anchor.surface_text: 1.  The case originated in two applications (nos. 40153/98 and 40160/98) against the Republic of Turkey lodged with the European Commission of Human Rights (“the Commission”) under former Article 25 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (“the Convention”) by eight Turkish nationals (“the applicants”): Mr Vedat Çetin, who lodged application no. 40153/98 on 5 January 1998, and Mr Mehmet Kaya, Mr Ismet Bakaç, Mr Ahmet Sünbül, Mr Zeynel Bagir, Mr Metin Dag, Mr Kemal Sahin and Mr Naif Kiliç, who jointly lodged application no. 40160/98 on 5 February 1998.

facts.text: The applicants are Turkish nationals and live in Diyarbakir. At the material time, they worked as journalists on Ülkede Gündem, a Turkish-language daily newspaper based in Istanbul.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  The applicants are Turkish nationals and live in Diyarbakir. At the material time, they worked as journalists on Ülkede Gündem, a Turkish-language daily newspaper based in Istanbul. Publication of the newspaper ceased on 24 October 1998 and it was replaced initially by Özgür Bakis and subsequently, on 27 April 2000, by another daily newspaper, 2 Binde Yeni Gündem. That newspaper was replaced on 31 May 2001 by a weekly periodical called Yedinci Gündem.

facts.text: Publication of the newspaper Ülkede Gündem ceased on 24 October 1998 and it was replaced initially by Özgür Bakis and subsequently by 2 Binde Yeni Gündem and then by Yedinci Gündem.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  The applicants are Turkish nationals and live in Diyarbakir. At the material time, they worked as journalists on Ülkede Gündem, a Turkish-language daily newspaper based in Istanbul. Publication of the newspaper ceased on 24 October 1998 and it was replaced initially by Özgür Bakis and subsequently, on 27 April 2000, by another daily newspaper, 2 Binde Yeni Gündem. That newspaper was replaced on 31 May 2001 by a weekly periodical called Yedinci Gündem.

facts.text: Mr Çetin wrote a column entitled “Notes from Diyarbakir” published on Tuesdays in Ülkede Gündem; Mr Bakaç was the newspaper's representative in Diyarbakir.

anchor.surface_text: 10.  At the material time one of the applicants, Mr Çetin, an independent journalist, wrote a column entitled “Notes from Diyarbakir” (Diyarbakir'dan Notlar), which was published on Tuesdays in Ülkede Gündem. Mr Bakaç was Ülkede Gündem's representative in Diyarbakir. He currently works as a press officer for the Diyarbakir Urban District Council.

facts.text: The other applicants had various roles: Mr Bagir is mayor of Lice, Mr Kaya is a lawyer, Mr Sahin and Mr Kiliç are school teachers, Mr Sünbül is a journalist with 7. Gündem, and Mr Dag is a press officer for Kayapinar Town Council.

anchor.surface_text: 11.  As for the other applicants, Mr Bagir is now the mayor of Lice, Mr Kaya is a lawyer and Mr Sahin and Mr Kiliç both teach in schools in eastern Turkey. Mr Sünbül continues to work as a journalist with the weekly publication 7. Gündem, while Mr Dag currently works as a press officer for Kayapinar Town Council.

facts.text: On 1 December 1997 the governor of the state of emergency region imposed a ban on the publication and distribution of Ülkede Gündem in that region.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  The main point at issue in the present case is a ban that was imposed on 1 December 1997 by the governor of the state of emergency region on the distribution of Ülkede Gündem in that region.

facts.text: Between September and November 1997, the distribution of Ülkede Gündem was impeded by security forces, leading to the governor imposing a ban on its publication and distribution in the state of emergency region.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: On 13 November 1997 the proprietor of Ülkede Gündem sent a letter to the Ministry of the Interior complaining about disruption to distribution and seeking compensation.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: On 19 November 1997 the governor of the state of emergency region replied to the proprietor stating his office was not responsible and enclosed seizure orders issued by Istanbul National Security Court judges.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: The Government produced seventy-two warrants issued by Istanbul National Security Court judges for seizure of various issues of Ülkede Gündem in September, November and December 1997.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: On 4 November 1997 Mr Bakaç and Mr Bagir lodged a criminal complaint with the Diyarbakir public prosecutor's office about disruption to the newspaper's distribution.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: On 25 November 1997 the public prosecutor's office ruled it had no power to deal with the complaint and referred it to the Diyarbakir Administrative Council under the Prosecution of Civil Servants Act.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: On 5 February 1998 the Diyarbakir Administrative Council held there was no case to answer in view of the seizure warrants issued by Istanbul National Security Court judges.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: The Diyarbakir Administrative Council's decision was upheld by the Supreme Administrative Court on 3 March 2000.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: On 4 December 1997 the Diyarbakir Security Directorate informed Mr Bakaç of the ban on publication and distribution of Ülkede Gündem in the state of emergency provinces.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: On 5 December 1997 the Tunceli Security Directorate wrote to the distributor Birlesik Basim Dagitim A.S. prohibiting publication and distribution of Ülkede Gündem in the state of emergency provinces.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: On 7 May 1999 the governor imposed a ban on the publication and distribution of Özgür Bakis, the daily newspaper that replaced Ülkede Gündem.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: On 1 June 2000 the governor issued an order prohibiting publication and distribution of 2 Binde Yeni Gündem in the state of emergency region.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: On 27 June 2001 the weekly publication Yedinci Gündem, successor to 2 Binde Yeni Gündem, was banned from publication and distribution in the state of emergency region.

anchor.surface_text: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

facts.text: A notice dated June 2000 shows that the governor imposed bans on the publication and distribution of seventeen periodicals, including Ülkede Gündem, Özgür Bakis and 2 Binde Yeni Gündem.

arguments.claim: The Court found that section 11(e) of the State of Emergency Act and Article 1 (a) of Legislative Decree no. 430 are drafted in very broad terms and grant the governor vast powers to impose administrative bans on publications, which may only be justified if a strict legal framework and effective judicial review exist to prevent abuse.

anchor.surface_text: section 11(e) of the State of Emergency Act and Article 1 (a) of Legislative Decree no. 430 are drafted in very broad terms and grant the governor of the state of emergency region vast powers to impose administrative bans on the publication and distribution of publications. Such prior restrictions are not, in principle, incompatible with the Convention. However, they may only be imposed if a particularly strict framework of legal rules regulating the scope of bans and ensuring the effectiveness of judicial review to prevent possible abuse is in place.

arguments.claim: The Court emphasized that the provisions conferring powers on the governor and the manner in which the rules are applied escape judicial scrutiny, depriving applicants of safeguards against abuse.
